:::info

La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

Control your **SOMA Smart Shades** (roller shade motors) and **SOMA Tilt**
(venetian blind motors) from Gladys, through the local HTTP API of your
**SOMA Connect** bridge.

> Unofficial integration, not affiliated with SOMA (Wazombi Labs). It has
> **never been tested with a real SOMA Connect**: it follows the API used by
> pysoma, the library of the maker. Feedback is welcome.

## How it works

- Gladys speaks **HTTP only** to SOMA Connect, on your local network (port
  3000). The Bluetooth link to the shades stays inside SOMA Connect: Gladys
  needs no Bluetooth. No account, no cloud.
- Each device listed by SOMA Connect becomes a **shutter** in the Discovery
  tab, with:
  - **Open / close**: open, close and **stop**;
  - **Position**: 0 % (closed) to 100 % (open);
  - **Battery** (%), read at most once an hour (each read wakes the shade).
- A **Tilt** turns the slats: 100 % = slats level (open), 0 % = closed
  downwards. A Tilt closed upwards (from the SOMA app) reads as closed; Gladys
  only closes downwards.

## Set up

1. Pair your shades with SOMA Connect in the SOMA app, and check that SOMA
   Connect is on your network.
2. Give SOMA Connect a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation).
3. In Gladys, type its **IP address** (port 3000 by default; another port:
   `192.168.1.50:3001`) and save. Press **Test the connection**.
4. In the **Discovery** tab, add the shades.

## Commands

- **Open and position** go to SOMA Connect within 3.5 s of your click,
  or are refused with nothing sent. Each shade takes its moves one at a time
  (4 waiting at most); different shades move side by side, so a scene can move
  all your shades at once.
- The acknowledgement says that **SOMA Connect accepted** the command. The
  position is **confirmed** only when a read shows it (within 2 %): the shade
  is read again 2, 5, 20, 45 and 90 s after a command. A shade that did not
  reach its position after the last read gets a warning badge and a line in
  the status.
- A command that may have reached SOMA Connect without an answer is told
  "sent, without confirmation", not "not sent".

### Stop

Stop goes first: it takes no queue, needs no read before it, has no option,
and goes through a pause asked by SOMA Connect and through the spacing of
the tries after a failure. It works right after a restart, before any read (the
address, the firmware and the shades are kept in `/data`). It cancels the moves
of that shade not sent yet: a move asked before a stop does not leave after it.
A read silent for a second is cut to give it the way.

A stop is refused, or not sent, in these cases only:

- the shade is unknown to the integration (never listed by SOMA Connect, and
  not kept in `/data`), or no address of SOMA Connect is typed nor kept;
- a move of that shade asked **after** the stop was accepted by SOMA Connect
  meanwhile (that move is what you asked last);
- SOMA Connect cannot be reached, or answers an error, during 3.5 s (tried
  every 250 ms): the stop is then **kept** (also in `/data`) and sent again
  once a minute (with or without the configuration of Gladys, to the address
  kept in `/data`), 3 times at most; the status and the badge say so, and say
  when it is given up.

When the reads 2 and 5 s after a stop show the shade still going the way it
went, the stop is sent again (3 times at most). Later reads never send a stop:
a move started from the SOMA app or a remote after a stop is left alone.

### Close

**Close** (and the position 0 %) is protective too: no queue (it replaces the
moves of that shade still waiting), no option, through a pause, before the
configuration of Gladys is read (address and shade kept in `/data`), tried
every 250 ms within 3.5 s; a move that was leaving is followed by the close
again. It is refused, or not sent, in these cases only:

- the shade is unknown to the integration, or no address of SOMA Connect is
  typed nor kept;
- a stop, or a move accepted by SOMA Connect, asked **after** it;
- SOMA Connect cannot be reached, or answers an error, during 3.5 s: unlike a
  stop, a close is then **not** kept nor sent again (not after a restart
  either).
- A close answered "not sent" or "refused" is never sent afterwards, not even
  behind the move that was leaving. A move it replaces is told so ("replaced by
  a close"), not "cancelled by a stop".

## Reads

- Every interval (60 s by default, 30 to 3600 s): the list of devices, then
  the position of each shade. Never sooner than the interval, except the reads
  after a command, even after a restart, a reconnection or the Test button.
- A shade out of Bluetooth reach of SOMA Connect is shown "not read" and its
  badge unreachable; the others go on.
- SOMA Connect unreachable: tried again after 30 s, 1, 2 then 5 min (never
  sooner than the interval). A "too many requests" (HTTP 429), or an error 5xx
  on the list of devices, pauses the moves (what Retry-After asks, 1 min to
  6 h; else 1 to 5 min; kept in `/data`) and the reads (never sooner than the
  interval anyway); the pause does not hold a stop nor a close. An error 5xx
  on one shade only marks that shade "not read".
- The URL form follows pysoma (`?mac=` for firmware 3, `/<mac>` otherwise);
  after a 404 the other form is tried at once, and the form that answered is
  kept for the next requests.
- A position is published only while it is recent; nothing old is published
  again as new.

## Limits

- One SOMA Connect, 32 devices at most.
- The light level of the solar panel is not read yet (its unit is not known).
- The type of a device (shade or Tilt) changed in SOMA Connect applies after a
  **Scan** in the Discovery tab.
- Never tested with a real SOMA Connect: the URL forms, the answers and the
  time SOMA Connect takes to answer are to be checked.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que SOMA Connect te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your SOMA shades in Gladys | `section` | No | Each SOMA Smart Shades or Tilt paired with your SOMA Connect becomes a shutter in the Discovery tab: open, close, stop, position and battery. Gladys only speaks HTTP to SOMA Connect on your local network (port 3000); the Bluetooth link to the shades stays inside SOMA Connect. No account, no cloud. Never tested with a real SOMA Connect yet. Unofficial, not affiliated with SOMA (Wazombi Labs). |
| Address of SOMA Connect | `string` | Sí | The local IP address of your SOMA Connect, like 192.168.1.50 (port 3000 by default; another port: 192.168.1.50:3001). Give it a fixed address in your router (DHCP reservation). |
| Read interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the position of each shade is read (30 to 3600 s). After a command, the shade is also read a few times while it moves. The battery is read at most once an hour. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the features of the shades added from now on. |

## Cómo instalar SOMA Connect en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: SOMA Connect aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-soma-connect:0.1.2`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-soma-connect](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-soma-connect).

SOMA Connect requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

SOMA Connect es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
